scope: Independent automated adversarial review of a proposed plan against pinned source. These are plan findings, not ten newly reproduced gameplay bugs. No runtime implementation or qualification was performed.

priority_meaning.P1: Resolve before the affected controls or transaction migration; the plan can otherwise permit a safety/authority regression or carry a known defect through its touched path.
priority_meaning.P2: Resolve contract, evidence or qualification ambiguity before its affected implementation or claim.
priority_meaning.P3: Correct source documentation accuracy; no demonstrated runtime impact.

findings.title: A direct session bridge can bypass live admission
findings.problem: request_resume(evidence) and session delegation do not identify the complete shell/activity gate or dispatch-time current authority. A stale snapshot or default zero sample is not authorization.
findings.consequence: An implementation could bypass selected source, generation, relevant profile, focus, radio-menu center, held-key or family readiness checks before a resumed tick.
findings.resolution: Minimal advisory status plus intent through the existing shell/activity and session chain; owner revalidation after any yield/defer; stale work cannot authorize another activity. Preserve guarded Fly/restart and family-specific readiness.

findings.title: The assumed shared status API and broad port are not established
findings.problem: VRC-01 calls a shared status contract existing, while actual consumers read different live fields and backend/status surfaces. The proposed full port precommits reset/restore/close and immutable capabilities before a real shared need.
findings.consequence: A generic facade could invent defaults, duplicate mutable safety authority, freeze dynamic availability or expand the migration before its first benefit is proven.
findings.resolution: Characterize existing per-family surfaces, then one fixed-wing status/pause/resume consumer. Unknown/support/readiness are distinct; dynamic availability is projected from owners. Defer broader methods and keep optional extractions independent.

findings.title: Input parity lacks temporal and real-consumer oracles
findings.problem: Broad keyboard/radio/gamepad, hold and capture parity does not specify event versus poll evidence, first accepted command, held key isolation, action release, AUX no-command or shaping ownership.
findings.consequence: Layer tests could pass while a bridge manufactures radio evidence, changes gamepad readiness, turns menu keys into flight input, reapplies curves or retracts a retained AUX target.
findings.resolution: Trace the actual route order, not an invented universal pipeline. Add explicit temporal and shaping cases with real affected consumers, retaining verified-gamepad first poll, trusted radio verification seed, keyboard capture, center versus command-OFF and per-family policies.

findings.title: Five known controls defects are not carried into affected gates
findings.problem: The plan acknowledges GCA-01 through GCA-05 but detailed characterization and migration order mention only the first three; a repair decision is not a repaired invariant in the touched path.
findings.consequence: Input/calibration extraction could retain known legacy lost updates or tiny-range wrong endpoints while being described as qualified consolidation.
findings.resolution: Carry all five pinned adverse witnesses into baseline disposition, then block only migrations touching the unresolved invariant until separate owning-track repair and repaired regression proof. Do not block unrelated status work or relabel adverse reproducer success as repair.

findings.title: Transaction and teardown guarantees are not universal
findings.problem: The broad reset/restore/close sketch and refusal-preserves-recording statement exceed the demonstrated common contract. Airship/quad reset notification can stop recorders before later refusal; tentative fixed-wing detach intentionally leaves recorders open.
findings.consequence: A common helper could close the surviving flight, misreport committed faults as rollback, discard pending data or claim preservation that a family never guaranteed.
findings.resolution: Defer these public operations; preserve owner-specific precommit/commit/notification/credit and exit policy. Add fault/reentry/tentative-detach/finalization/worker cases only when those seams move. Stronger guarantees require separate repairs.

findings.title: Source-moving replay gates need an identity-aware workflow
findings.problem: The plan asks for exact-state/replay preservation without explaining how a source-moving PR changes the solver fingerprint. Interpreting this as old-log exact replay on changed source would be refused; candidate mode has domain and backend limits.
findings.consequence: Implementers could bypass identity guards, require impossible evidence, call a candidate experiment exact or mistake reference candidate replay for native qualification.
findings.resolution: Exact baseline on matching original identity; exact comparison only when identity genuinely matches, otherwise supported explicit candidate or owner differential/blocked. Report completeness/mode/solver_changed/backend and separately qualify native. Preserve already acknowledged post-conditioning limitations.

findings.title: Test names and process success do not prove the promised route
findings.problem: The proposed examples include a golden helper as if executable, no completion marker in the sample runner command, and fixture names without declaring real/fake boundaries, retained tapes or current execution status.
findings.consequence: A partial run, fake-only route, short synthetic tape or historical adverse witness could be mistaken for complete control qualification, particularly given five unqualified prior suites.
findings.resolution: Forty proposed case rows bind owners, triggers, oracles, test starting points and evidence; all UNRUN. Require real affected consumers, exact terminal roster/diagnostics, fresh isolated data/imports and current receipts. Preserve 22/27 historical limits and required CI.

findings.title: Direct, managed and family control policies need explicit scope
findings.problem: Shared service/admission wording is too broad for supported service-free direct routes, managed V2 versus legacy save/read behavior, per-family throttle/curve policy and static versus configurable controls. Airship wording also says centered throttle instead of low throttle.
findings.consequence: An extraction could introduce a mandatory service, alter active-but-unsaved calibration behavior, invent unreadable-legacy-reader guarantees, change quad fallback/rate policy or promise unimplemented remapping/menu support.
findings.resolution: Inventory supported routes and preserve the real policy for each; managed rollback differs from direct activate-before-save. Explicitly retain verified gamepad readiness, radio challenge rules, fixed controls, low-throttle/centered-yaw airship and held quad fallback. Future behavior improvements remain separately owned.

findings.title: Control response and support claims need their own measured gates
findings.problem: Workload timing and generic platform/device language do not directly catch a new input queue, stale sample or lost setup/recovery usability, and do not identify applicable transport, physical, export and soak rows.
findings.consequence: A faster microbenchmark or clean synthetic path could be presented as better control feel or wider compatibility without matching evidence.
findings.resolution: Use existing F6 and controller/DT owners: event/sample/first-command/visible-response traces, paired recorded source/workload comparisons, actual hardware/transport/package rows, scoped soak, accessible EN/ES recovery and pilot evidence. No new speedup or arbitrary latency budget is claimed.

findings.title: All ten source line counts include a phantom final line
findings.problem: Every inventory line count is one greater than the pinned source's actual line count; blob IDs and function counts are correct.
findings.consequence: Inspection metrics are not reproducible as stated, though there is no demonstrated runtime impact or complexity/performance conclusion.
findings.resolution: Regenerate using UTF-8 splitlines without a phantom final empty line; correct plan/table/JSON, retain original revision and add reproducible static checks.
